It is often useful to describe chemical reactions using energy diagrams. A spontaneous chemical reaction has a negative free energy change, so the reaction occurs with a net release of free energy. The spontaneity of a process may depend on the temperature of the system. Phase transitions, for example, will proceed spontaneously in one direction or the other depending on the temperature of the substance in question. Likewise, some chemical reactions can also exhibit temperature-dependent spontaneities.
